ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, (a) is a circuit composed of input voltage Ui, diode VD, and resistor R connected in series; (b) is the diode forward volt-ampere characteristic curve, the horizontal axis is diode voltage u/V, and the vertical axis is current i/mA. The curve rises rapidly after about 0.5 V, and near u about 0.6 V the corresponding current is about 4 mA. Reasoning: From the given Ui = 4.6 V and R = 1 kΩ, the series circuit satisfies i = (4.6 - u) / 1 kΩ. If current is expressed in mA, then the load line is i = 4.6 - u. Comparing this load line with the diode characteristic curve in figure (b), the intersection is at u about 0.6 V, at which time the load-line current is about 4.6 - 0.6 = 4.0 mA, consistent with the diode curve reading of about 4 mA on the figure. Therefore, the forward voltage drop of the diode is about 0.6 V.
